definitions.meaning: one of the four seasons of the year, the one after winter
a source of water rising from the ground, as in a hot or mineral one

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the season between winter and summer, and a natural source where water wells up.

parts.note: credit here means belief, so a doubter who will not believe, not a stingy lender

explanation.definitionFit: A doubter refuses to believe claims; 'credit' suggests money but means belief.

clue.text: After a drink, sailor gets up for a dance

indicators.note: after places the sailor's letters following the drink

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

indicators.note: in a down light, gets up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: Having had a drink, a sailor rises to dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets up' works because this is a down entry: the sailor reads from bottom to top. AB, an able seaman, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban ballroom dance with a lively rhythm; one example of a dance.

parts.note: favouring one's relatives, as in handing out jobs to family members

explanation.definitionFit: Showing favouritism to relatives is nepotism; 'Relatively' means 'towards relatives', not 'comparatively'.

parts.note: rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Someone drifts off from the glow of the streetlamps into the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to wander off course or away from the group, so the verb forms match.

clue.text: Novel hat for a Parisian model

definitions.meaning: a book by George du Maurier, 1894
a soft felt hat with a narrow brim
the heroine of that book, an artist's model in Paris

explanation.walkthrough: The 1894 novel by George du Maurier is named after its heroine, an artist's model in Paris; the felt hat became fashionable after its stage version.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name serves the book, its Paris-model heroine, and the felt hat named after the play.

clue.text: Bill joins detectives sent out after crashes?

indicators.note: joins puts the bill and the detectives side by side

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

indicators.note: out means the letters of sent are disordered

explanation.surface: Police called to a series of crashes, a bill arriving afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent out' gives ENTS, an anagram of SENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Crashes are examples of mishaps; the question mark flags definition by example.

parts.note: to sit an exam is to take it
doing well, thriving

explanation.surface: A student sits a test about a thriving poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Edith Sitwell was a 20th-century English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Sitwell, and her brothers Osbert and Sacheverell, were English writers; she is best known for verse.

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
cement is a mortar used to bind bricks

explanation.surface: Builders test mortar to add extra strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra support or added troops strengthen something; the word names that addition.

parts.note: a broad happy smile, and also, read whimsically, a smile from the sun: a shaft of sunlight

explanation.definitionFit: A broad grin is described with this word, which also names a shaft of sunlight, so a sunny smile fits both.

clue.text: Bet policies are revised, nonetheless, in referendum

indicators.note: revised means the letters of the fodder are reworked into a new order
read as 'none-the-less', it says to drop the letter that looks like zero, nothing, from the fodder

explanation.surface: Despite wagers that party lines have shifted, a public vote goes ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonetheless' looks like a link meaning 'however', but it splits as none (O) less: remove one O from BETPOLICIES, then 'revised' rearranges the remaining ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a direct vote by the whole electorate on a single question.

clue.text: A trust set up by the royal family

indicators.note: set up here means arranged afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A charitable trust has been founded by the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reads as 'founded' but tells you to rearrange A TRUST.
explanation.definitionFit: The dynasty that ruled Scotland and later England in the 1600s; a royal house name.

clue.text: Unimportant persons found after well-planned murders?

definitions.meaning: people of no consequence or status
a perfect killing leaves no corpses to discover, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: People of no importance are called this, and split into 'no bodies' it is what a clever murderer leaves behind.

clue.text: He doesn't have to be smart to fool the birds

definitions.text: He doesn't have to be smart to fool the birds

parts.words: He doesn't have to be smart to fool the birds
parts.note: a straw figure in a field wears old ragged clothes, not smart ones

explanation.definitionFit: The figure dressed in tattered clothes in a field deceives crows; 'smart' plays on both well-dressed and clever.

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question whether a musical performance lacks emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' looks musical but rearranges IS RECITAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical, hard-headed view sees things as they are, without sentiment.

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, so nil

explanation.surface: A fondness for a deep blue colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the indigo plant and the blue dye made from it, a crossword-familiar word.

clue.text: Get weapon out but don't win

definitions.meaning: to pull a gun or sword from its holster or sheath
to end a game level, neither side the victor

explanation.definitionFit: Unsheathing a sword is drawing it, and a match tied with neither side ahead is a draw.

definitions.meaning: a round wooden block with holes used to tighten a ship's shrouds

explanation.definitionFit: An unerring marksman is called this, and on a sailing ship it is a pierced block that tensions the rigging.

clue.text: Lock in the experts, they're only pretending to work

indicators.note: in tells us the lock of hair sits inside the word for experts

parts.note: aces are experts or top performers
a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: An order to shut the specialists away, as if they only feign working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' looks like a verb but is a noun: a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage performers earn their living by pretending to be other people, a witty paraphrase of the job.

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to cede is to give up territory

explanation.surface: An army surrendered ground and fell back.
explanation.definitionFit: Withdrew or moved back, both past tense verbs of moving away.

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium, a colourless gas in the periodic table

explanation.definitionFit: Helium, symbol He, is a colourless gas and one of the chemical substances in the periodic table.

clue.text: I join Bond's boss arranging raid above ground level

indicators.note: join places I next to the boss's letter

parts.note: M is the head of MI6 in the James Bond stories

indicators.note: arranging tells us to reorder the letters of raid

explanation.surface: An agent teams up with the spymaster to plan an air raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond's boss' is M, head of the secret service in the James Bond novels; the reordered word sits after him and the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something up in the sky, off the ground, is said to be in this position.

parts.note: a belief against hitting anyone, which the surface makes look like a trade-union position on strikes

explanation.definitionFit: Opposition to violence and war means refusing to strike a blow; 'striking' suggests industrial action instead.

clue.text: Capital in credit in Norfolk resort

indicators.note: in places the capital city inside the abbreviation for credit

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: Money is invested on credit at a seaside town in eastern England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money but is a capital city. Norfolk is a county on England's east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Cromer is a seaside town on the north Norfolk coast, famous for its crabs and pier.

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
an eye is what looks

explanation.surface: A tidy, attractive flower is praised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' means cattle, not tidy; 'looker' is an eye, not a beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox-eye daisy is a large wild white daisy of meadows.

clue.text: Held in check, fell behind the others

indicators.note: behind places the word for fell after the word for the others

parts.note: the rest means the remaining ones
rain fell, or it rained

explanation.surface: A runner, reined in, dropped back behind the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like a stumble but is the past tense of falling rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Being kept under control or curbed is the sense; held back by restraint, matching a past participle.

parts.note: female sheep, and also four compass quarters, east, west, east and south, written letter by letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' looks like living space for sheep, but the compass quarters E, W, E and S spell the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Female sheep go by this name, and the same letters spell out four compass quarters in a row.

clue.text: Repeat prescription once more, not involving the doctor

indicators.note: a prescription is something made up, so the letters are mixed into a new form
not involving means the doctor's letters are removed from the phrase

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

explanation.surface: A patient asks for the same medicine again without seeing the GP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not involving' takes MO out of ONCE MORE, leaving ONCERE, and 'prescription' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra performance demanded by the audience is a repeat of an item already played.

clue.text: The coming of the Christian faith

definitions.text: The coming of the Christian faith

parts.words: The coming of the Christian faith
parts.note: the arrival of Christ, celebrated in the church season before Christmas

explanation.definitionFit: The word means an arrival, and in the church calendar marks the awaited birth of Christ.
